responses.sql: SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating

assumptions.assumption: The per-film ratio rental_rate / rental_duration is averaged across films (AVG of the ratio), not computed as AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration). Division is done in floating/decimal arithmetic without rounding.
'More than 20.99' is a strict inequality (replacement_cost > 20.99), so films at exactly 20.99 are excluded.

responses.sql: SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating;

assumptions.assumption: Films with a NULL length are excluded from the length average, which is the default behavior of AVG. The rental_rate/rental_duration average is computed per film, then averaged across the films in each rating, not as a ratio of sums.
The filter replacement_cost > 20.99 is strict, so films costing exactly 20.99 are excluded.

responses.sql: SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating

assumptions.assumption: AVG ignores NULL lengths and NULL ratios by default; rental_duration is never 0 (values are 3 to 7), so there is no division by zero. Films with a NULL rating, if any, would form their own group, but the data shows 5 rating levels.
